title: Property of the descended finite affine presentation
statement:
Every chart, overlap open, and overlap map in the constructed raw datum
base changes to its named counterpart in $\mathsf R_X$.

proof.text: For a chart, isPullback_baseChangeCone_π identifies its limit projection square as a pullback. Transport this square along the retained chartComparison and eqToIso of rawChart_eq, using IsPullback.of_iso. The equation chartComparison_snd identifies the remaining structure map with the inclusion of the named chart followed by f. This is the first conjunct. The chart isomorphism is already data of the fixed raw datum, so its construction from the affine algebra need not be repeated.

proof.text: For each overlap, retain its paired morphism choice M. Its baseCompact, baseQS, leftCompact, leftQS and the finite-presentation instance fields supply the hypotheses of nagataMorphismDescends. Apply that theorem to M.forwardChoice and M.backwardChoice, then rewrite using M.forward_eq and M.backward_eq. This gives the recovery equation at each chosen morphism stage.

proof.text: Let g be either chosen finite-stage map, T its recorded transport to the raw stage, and φ its limit map. Precompose T.map_eq with the source limit projection. Naturality of both baseChangeCones and Step 4 show that π_raw≫T.map.left and φ≫π_raw agree after the target transition to the chosen stage. Postcompose this equality with that target model’s first pullback projection; baseChangeDiagram_map_fst makes these the first projections of the two maps into the raw target. The over-base equation T.map.w, baseChangeCone_π_app_snd and the choice’s limitOver give equality of the second projections. Pullback.hom_ext gives the raw-stage equation. Apply this in both directions and assemble it with Steps 1 and 3.

split_report.summary: Repaired the returned long Step 5 without changing the statement, Lean record or Steps 1-4. Its hidden qcqs and transported-open compactness arguments now cite existing permanence statements in short steps. One statement-only lemma isolates finite presentation of quasi-compact opens in base changes of affine finitely presented charts. Morphism descent is applied with every hypothesis verified, followed by the elementary naturality comparison already established in Step 2. Corrected the retained attempt's unlogged search records by using real recorded queries and eliminated its redundant common-stage and transport nodes.

tool_uses.why: The generic fibre-product universal property gives the explicit inverse and naturality of iterated base change; no unit-specific theorem replaces this definition.
The affine tensor-product description converts the chart algebra comparison into the scheme comparison, with the specified projections; no Nagata-unit node states this generic fact.
Affineness under base change, affineness over an affine target and qcqs of an affine morphism are generic inputs to common-stage bookkeeping, not another approximation route.
Clause (2) propagates qcqs from the fixed initial base along affine transitions; no unit-local node states the generic permanence fact.
Inverse images under the affine chart transitions preserve compactness of the descended overlap opens; this generic topological permanence statement is not a change of approximation route.

Step 8 matches Stacks 01ZM(2) exactly: S_w is qcqs and both overlap models are of finite presentation over it. The new node lem-nagata-qc-open-basechanged-affine-chart-fp is true, by the argument 01TQ, then 01TU for V into S, 01TR, 01TS, X_T qcqs, then 01TU for W into X_T, then 01TR. proof.text:
Apply the corresponding property lemma to each finite-presentation chart,
quasi-compact overlap, and overlap morphism. There are only finitely many
objects, and the common upper bound transports all of them to one stage
without changing their base changes.
